name: inprocess-obi-tlul-gpio-w1c-f5
description: One Ibex RVFI OBI CPU reaches one real OpenTitan TL-UL GPIO in one process and takes its real level interrupt: the F5 firmware writes INTR_ENABLE=1 then INTR_TEST=1, the RTL latches INTR_STATE[0] and drives intr_gpio_o[0], the ISR reads INTR_STATE at 0x0 and clears it with a write-one-to-clear of the same bit, and the level really falls and stays low.
notes: One OBI CPU (Ibex RVFI) reaches one TL-UL target at 0x40004000 behind the real beat_to_tlul adapter; the profile's own protocol is tl-ul/1, so no APB3 or Wishbone target is in this build.

The behavior file configs/behaviors/opentitan_gpio_w1c_f5.json is the declaration: it names the RTL's own output intr_gpio_o (gpio.sv:35), the INTR_STATE status word at 0x00, cause bit 0, the trigger sequence INTR_ENABLE(0x04)=1 then INTR_TEST(0x08)=1, and the clear INTR_STATE(0x00)=1.

This is the repository's first F5 clear that is a real write-one-to-clear which HOLDS low: gpio.sv instantiates prim_intr_hw with the default IntrT="Event", so new_event (the INTR_TEST/ted event) sets the state and nothing re-asserts it until the next event; the handler's W1C therefore drops intr_gpio_o[0] for good. rv_timer's INTR_STATE0 cannot do this (IntrT="Status", re-driven every cycle) and remains on its compare-update clear.

Window: the profile's own 128-byte gpio register window (address.window_size 0x80, alignment 128) at 0x40004000..0x40004080, the same base the TL-UL rv_timer scenario uses. It clears the RAM image 0x10000..0x30000 and the 4 GiB bound.

The gpio profile declares no dir-resolved pad word (its external_pins roles are in/out/en/strap_en), so no pin model is declared and none is required; the interrupt is raised through the register interface (INTR_TEST), not through a pad.
No DMA is declared, so F6 is refused as unsupported-f6:no-dma-model:TL-UL.
This file declares the scenario; the run under runs/p2-irq-20261103/ is the evidence, and it claims only what its case lines read from the device.

fixed_inputs own the two declared single-word pin inputs: gpio.pins/in=0 (no pad is driven high, so no pad event can contribute) and gpio.pins/strap_en=0 (strap sampling disabled). The register-interface INTR_TEST path is the only event source this build declares.
